title: Measurement Conversions
description: Master measurement conversions for Class 4 Maths — km to m, kg to g, L to mL, hours to minutes. Real-life word problems with step-by-step solutions, 10 MCQs and 6 IMO questions.

topics.title: Length Conversions (km, m, cm)
topics.concept:
The metric system uses powers of 10 for all conversions — making them easy with multiplication and division.

Key Conversions for Length:

  • 1 km = 1,000 m (multiply by 1,000 to convert km to m)
  • 1 m = 100 cm (multiply by 100 to convert m to cm)
  • 1 km = 1,00,000 cm

Converting from larger to smaller unit: MULTIPLY.
Converting from smaller to larger unit: DIVIDE.

Memory trick: King Henry Died By Drinking Chocolate Milk — Kilo, Hecto, Deca, Base, Deci, Centi, Milli.

topics.title: Weight and Capacity Conversions (kg, g, L, mL)
topics.concept:
Weight (Mass):
1 kilogram (kg) = 1,000 grams (g)

Capacity:
1 litre (L) = 1,000 millilitres (mL)

Both use the same conversion factor: x 1,000 for the larger-to-smaller direction.

In Indian context: a bag of sugar = 1 kg = 1,000 g. A large water bottle = 1 L = 1,000 mL.

topics.title: Time Conversions
topics.concept:
Time conversions do NOT follow powers of 10 — so we must memorize these relationships:

  • 1 hour = 60 minutes
  • 1 minute = 60 seconds
  • 1 day = 24 hours
  • 1 week = 7 days

To convert hours to minutes: multiply by 60.
To convert minutes to hours: divide by 60.

For elapsed time (how long something took): convert start and end to the same unit, then subtract.

examples.problem: Convert 150 minutes to hours and minutes.
examples.solution: 60 minutes = 1 hour. 150 / 60 = 2 hours with remainder 30. Answer: 2 hours 30 minutes.

examples.problem: A movie starts at 2:30 PM and ends at 4:45 PM. How long is it in minutes?
examples.solution: From 2:30 to 4:30 = 2 hours = 120 minutes. From 4:30 to 4:45 = 15 minutes. Total = 120 + 15 = 135 minutes.

recap: 1 minute = 60 seconds; 1 day = 24 hours; 1 week = 7 days
For elapsed time: find time from start to end
Time conversions use x60 (larger to smaller) and /60 (smaller to larger)

topics.title: Mixed Measurement Word Problems
topics.concept:
Many real-life problems combine different units or require multiple steps. Always:

  • Step 1: Identify the units given and the unit needed
  • Step 2: Convert all measurements to the same unit
  • Step 3: Perform the required calculation
  • Step 4: Express answer in appropriate unit

Common mistakes to avoid: forgetting to convert before adding, mixing up kg and g in the same calculation.

examples.problem: Riya ran 2.5 km in the morning and 1,750 m in the evening. Total distance?
A water tank has 12 L 500 mL. After using 3 L 750 mL and adding 5 L 250 mL, how much is left?
A train journey starts at 8:45 AM and ends at 2:15 PM. Duration in minutes?
examples.solution: 8:45 AM to 2:15 PM = 5 hours 30 minutes = (5 x 60) + 30 = 300 + 30 = 330 minutes.

recap: Always convert to the same unit before adding or subtracting
Large to small: multiply; Small to large: divide
For time: hours and minutes must be handled separately before adding
Always check if your answer is in the correct unit
